messages:
noah (devex): FYI: customer reports `redwoodctl` installed via MSI but `redwoodctl update` fails with "command not found" from their PowerShell after restart. they also say first-run quickstart claims auth succeeded but sample app 403s.
ivy (eng-platform): do we have installer telemetry from that MSI run? which channel/version?
noah (devex): attached in the ticket: MSI 2.3.1, Windows 11. They launched via Start Menu shortcut and used the button to open a dev terminal.
support-bot: ticket logs (sanitized):
```
INFO installer: created shim at C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin\redwoodctl.exe
INFO postinstall: attempted to add user PATH via registry HKCU\Environment
WARNING postinstall: failed to write HKCU registry: access denied
INFO login: success, token saved to C:\Users\alice\.config\redwood\profiles\default.json
```
omar (eng-runtime): registry write failing explains PATH not being updated for the user. but that wouldn't break the Start Menu shortcut itself. Two separate issues: 1) PATH shim missing for shells opened later, 2) token not picked up by sample app (403).
zara (devops): installer should elevate only where necessary. HKCU writes normally don't need admin, but some corp machines lock HKCU. fallback is to write a per-user shim into %LOCALAPPDATA%\redwood\bin and add a shell-profile instruction in postinstall (shell rc) if registry fails.
ivy (eng-platform): for the auth 403, could this be the same root cause as our WSL issues where Start Menu runs a different user context, or the sample app using a different profile? do they run sample in `devapp` container?
 o mar (eng-runtime): customer said they launched the quickstart node sample from the Start Menu -> "Open in Developer PowerShell" which spawns a new process with a different environment (corporate shell init). If PATH shim wasn't present in that shell, maybe an older CLI on PATH was invoked (bundled via chocolatey) which reads legacy config location and finds no token -> 403.
noah (devex): repro steps we asked them to run: `where redwoodctl`, `redwoodctl --version`, `type redwoodctl` in PS. they returned `C:\tools\choco\bin\redwoodctl.exe` and version 2.2.0. So yep, old binary.
zara (devops): action: installer should remove old chocolatey shims if detected, or at least warn and print a clear postinstall message: "Old redwoodctl on PATH at C:\tools\choco\bin\redwoodctl.exe may shadow this install." Also document known corporate shell init pitfalls.
ivy (eng-platform): on the CLI side, we should make `redwoodctl login` verify that the running binary is the one on PATH for interactive shells and warn if a different binary would be found in other shells. Maybe print: "Note: different shells may resolve a different redwoodctl on PATH; run `which -a redwoodctl` to verify."
omar (eng-runtime): for token behavior, we should ensure the CLI writes token atomically and emits an explicit success message that includes the canonical resolved path and a verification step: e.g., "Saved token to /home/alice/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json (exists: yes)". If the file write succeeded but another binary can't read it due to legacy config paths, add a short diagnostics command `redwoodctl diag-profiles` that prints both XDG and legacy lookup paths and which one the current binary will use.
zara (devops): installer changes: - try per-user shim fallback - if registry PATH write fails, append a short C:\Users\%USERNAME%\.config\redwood\bin addition to PowerShell profile (if writable) and print instructions.
noah (devex): short-term support workaround for the customer: 1) `where redwoodctl` to ensure correct binary 2) run `C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin\redwoodctl.exe login` from the shell they use to start the sample 3) verify `redwoodctl profile show --active` 4) restart the sample.
ivy (eng-platform): i'll open GH issue GH#5012: "MSI postinstall PATH shim can be shadowed by older installs and HKCU write failures; improve fallback and diagnostics" and assign to zara for installer + omar for CLI diag.
support-bot: created GH#5012
noah (devex): thanks. i'll paste the three-line workaround into the ticket and add the quickstart note: "If you use corporate shells, run login from the same shell your app runs in." :memo:
